target_columns.name: region
target_columns.transformation: COALESCE(policies.region, 'UNKNOWN') to replace NULL region with literal 'UNKNOWN'

target_columns.name: collection_delay_days
target_columns.transformation: DATEDIFF(DAY, period_start, collected_date), i.e. collected_date - period_start in days

target_columns.name: aging_bucket
target_columns.transformation: Bucket of DATEDIFF(DAY, period_start, collected_date) recomputed independently per branch: <=0 -> 'On Time', 1-30 -> '1-30 Days', 31-60 -> '31-60 Days', else -> '60+ Days'

quirks: The day-delay CASE expression recomputes DATEDIFF(DAY, period_start, collected_date) three separate times instead of referencing a single computed value; migration must ensure all three evaluations stay logically identical (e.g. compute once and reuse) to avoid subtle divergence.

If collected_date is NULL, DATEDIFF returns NULL; none of the WHEN conditions evaluate true (NULL comparisons are not TRUE), so the row silently falls into the ELSE branch and is misclassified as '60+ Days' rather than being flagged as uncollected/unknown.
Negative delays (collected_date before period_start) are bucketed into 'On Time' via the <=0 condition rather than being treated as an anomaly or excluded.
COALESCE(pol.region, 'UNKNOWN') masks NULL region values with the literal string 'UNKNOWN' -- must preserve this exact sentinel value, not drop/filter the rows.

INNER JOIN to policies silently drops any premiums rows whose policy_id has no matching policy -- no outer join or audit of orphaned premiums, so reconciliation must account for this implicit filtering.
Bucket boundaries are inclusive/exclusive in a specific way (<=0, 1-30, 31-60, 60+) -- off-by-one errors at the 0/1, 30/31, and 60/61 boundaries must be avoided during PySpark translation.
